title: VESPER: Online Learning of Free Energies with a Multi-Tempered Variational Objective
abstract:
arXiv:2611.00401v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computing molecular free-energy landscapes over collective variables (CVs) is central to understanding molecular mechanisms, but poses a difficult learning problem without training data available a priori. Samples of the marginal CV distribution must be generated by molecular dynamics (MD), whose trajectories can remain trapped in metastable states and rarely cross the free-energy barriers governing conformational changes or chemical reactions. We introduce VESPER, which couples the generation of these samples to neural-network-driven free-energy learning: MD supplies configurations for learning, while the evolving model biases the MD to accelerate exploration and generate further training data. VESPER minimizes a single variational objective that is convex in the free energy and can combine several tempering levels, each flattening the free-energy landscape to promote barrier crossing. Every level has the same physical free energy as its minimizer, allowing data from all levels to train one shared model without reweighting. Learning uses the difference in mean parameter gradients between biased MD configurations and auxiliary walkers that explore the flattened model in CV space. We prove conditional convergence of the coupled overdamped population dynamics without replica exchange under log-Sobolev and Polyak-Lojasiewicz assumptions. VESPER matches or improves on established enhanced-sampling methods on alanine dipeptide and yields self-consistent free-energy reconstructions from three to six CVs on alanine tetrapeptide. For methane dehydrogenation on Ni(511) with a machine-learned interatomic potential, it recovers two-CV Boltzmann marginals and a reactant-to-saddle free-energy difference along a three-CV path, both qualitatively consistent with the lower-dimensional reference. It also samples RMSD-defined folded and unfolded regions of chignolin while biasing seventeen CVs.
relevance_reason: Key author: Eric Vanden-Eijnden

title: COACH: Toward the performance limit of traditional hybrid density functionals for molecular chemistry
abstract:
arXiv:2603.23466v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) offers an exceptional balance between accuracy and efficiency, but practical density functional approximations face an unavoidable trade-off among simplicity, accuracy, and transferability. Here we present a systematic functional-development protocol that combines constraint enforcement, flexible functional forms, and modern optimization within a predefined application domain and functional class. Applying this strategy to the range-separated hybrid (RSH) meta-GGA framework, we obtain the carefully optimized and appropriately constrained hybrid (COACH) functional. Across broad molecular benchmarks, COACH improves both accuracy and transferability relative to leading RSH meta-GGAs, including \(\omega\)B97M-V, while retaining the computational practicality of its rung. These results suggest that COACH comes closer to the performance limit of traditional hybrid meta-GGA functionals for general molecular ground-state chemistry. Further substantial progress will likely require richer nonlocal or orbital-dependent information than is available from semilocal density ingredients combined with simple exact-exchange mixing.
relevance_reason: Key author: Martin Head-Gordon

title: Continuous SUN (Stable, Unique, and Novel) Metric for Generative Modeling of Inorganic Crystals
abstract:
arXiv:2510.12405v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: To address pressing scientific challenges such as climate change, increasingly sophisticated generative models are being developed to efficiently sample the large chemical space of potential functional materials. The proliferation of these models has necessitated the establishment of rigorous evaluation metrics. While uniqueness (U), novelty (N), and stability (S) of samples serve as standard metrics, their current formulations show several limitations. U and N rely on binary comparisons of crystals, rendering them dependent on heuristic thresholds, incapable of quantifying the degree of similarity, sensitive to atomic coordinate perturbations, and not invariant to sample permutation. Similarly, the binary assessment of S risks a premature exclusion of marginally unstable yet potentially novel candidates. These limitations are addressed by making the aforementioned metrics continuous. Furthermore, we integrate them into a unified metric ``continuous SUN" (cSUN), which offers a smoother score distribution and greater tunability than the conventional binary SUN metric. Experimental results demonstrate that our continuous metrics provide granular insights into sample distributions and secondarily serve as a soft screening score for selecting samples for further analysis. Finally, the use of cSUN as a reward signal in reinforcement learning is explored, showing that its adjustable weighting scheme effectively enhances sample diversity and convergence to a better optima in a Chemeleon2 case study.
relevance_reason: Key author: Aron Walsh

title: Kernel-Gradient Drifting Models
abstract:
arXiv:2605.10727v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We propose kernel-gradient drifting, a one-step generative modeling framework that replaces the fixed Euclidean displacement direction in drifting models with directions induced by the kernel itself. Standard drifting is attractive because it enables fast, high-quality generation without distilling a large pretrained diffusion model, but its theory is currently understood mainly for Gaussian kernels, where the drift coincides with smoothed score matching and is identifiable. Our gradient-based reformulation exposes this score-based structure for general kernels: the resulting drift is the score difference between kernel-smoothed data and model distributions, yielding identifiability for characteristic kernels and a smoothed-KL descent interpretation of the smoothed drifting dynamics. Since kernel gradients are intrinsic tangent vectors, the same construction extends naturally to Riemannian manifolds and to discrete data via the Fisher-Rao geometry of the probability simplex. Across spherical geospatial data, promoter DNA and molecule generation, kernel-gradient drifting enables state-of-the-art one-step generation beyond the Euclidean setting without distillation. Code is available \href{https://github.com/jcarrascopollo/kgd_thesis}{here}.
relevance_reason: Key author: Max Welling

title: GPU infrastructure for ML/MM with electrostatic embedding for enzyme chemistry
abstract:
arXiv:2611.02315v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a fully GPU-native framework for machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) enhanced sampling simulations with electrostatic embedding, demonstrated on an enzymatic reaction. The framework combines a JAX port of the pretrained MACE-POLAR-1-M model, an electrostatic embedding scheme compatible with the MACE-POLAR architecture, and integration with JAX-MD and PLUMED-JAX for end-to-end compiled enhanced sampling. The implementation is developed using GPT-6.1-Sol within Codex, with reasoning effort set to high. Using replica exchange umbrella sampling, we calculate the free energy profile of nucleophilic substitution in haloalkane dehalogenase in approximately 200 H100 GPU hours, treating the entire protein and reactants with MACE-POLAR-1-M-JAX and most of the solvent with molecular mechanics.
relevance_reason: GPU-native ML/MM with MACE-POLAR, JAX-MD, and PLUMED-JAX replica-exchange umbrella sampling computes an enzyme free-energy profile, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: FACTO: fast atom-centered tensor operator for accurate and efficient foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials
abstract:
arXiv:2611.03276v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-throughput inference remains a central challenge for equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials. Here we introduce FACTO, an atom-centered equivariant architecture that confines evolving learned state and dense channel mixing to atoms, expressing neighbor interactions as fully fusible reductions. We complement this design with custom register-accumulated aggregation kernels and tensor-core FP32 emulation, accelerating inference while retaining FP32-level energy conservation under emulated arithmetic in molecular dynamics. Comprehensive evaluations on Matbench Discovery, MLIP Arena and MatCalc demonstrate high throughput alongside strong predictive accuracy and physical reliability. On Matbench Discovery, the four FACTO-OAM variants show top-tier performance by overall rank sum among 46 models with complete scores, advancing the accuracy-throughput Pareto frontier. On MLIP Arena, FACTO achieves state- of-the-art stability under extreme heating and compression, alongside high fidelity in hydrogen combustion. On MatCalc, FACTO outperforms the compared baselines in structural and elastic predictions while retaining competitive accuracy for energetic and thermal properties.
relevance_reason: FACTO is an equivariant MLIP architecture benchmarked on Matbench Discovery, MLIP Arena, and MatCalc and validated in MD, satisfying (a)-(c) as MLIP development/benchmarking.

title: Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential for the Mo-S-Al-O System
abstract:
arXiv:2611.02403v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a machine-learned neuroevolution potential (NEP) for the Mo-S-Al-O system, targeting MoS$_2$ heteroepitaxy on c-plane sapphire, $\alpha$-Al$_2$O$_3$(0001). The potential is trained on 63,611 PBE+D3 structures distilled from about 1.1 million curated density-functional-theory (DFT) configurations, using an energy-difference loss function that directly targets interfacial and orientation-dependent energies. On held-out data, the energy and force errors are 29 meV/atom and 0.23 eV/$\mathring{A}$. Validated against DFT on a suite of physical properties, the NEP reproduces the lattice constants within 0.3 %, the elastic constants within 17 %, the phonon dispersions with mean deviations below 2.5%, and the surface energies within 1.3 %. At the MoS$_2$/sapphire interface, it reproduces the adhesion energy minimum within 0.8 %, the interfacial energy within 2.2 % and the most stable orientation of the monolayer. It preserves the DFT-predicted energetic ordering of edges, point defects (Spearman $\rho$ = 0.995) and mirror-twin boundaries ($\rho$ = 1.0), and reproduces tilt grain-boundary energies within 8 % ($\rho$ = 0.98) and stacking-fault energy barriers within 14 %. The resulting potential enables future studies of the atomic-scale mechanisms of defect formation in two-dimensional heteroepitaxy.
relevance_reason: Development and benchmarking of a neuroevolution MLIP for Mo-S-Al-O satisfies (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP training, and (c) applied atomistic simulation.

title: PLUMED-JAX: GPU-native enhanced sampling for atomistic simulations
abstract:
arXiv:2611.00483v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present PLUMED-JAX, an AI-assisted adaptation of selected PLUMED collective variables, umbrella sampling, and metadynamics for JAX-based atomistic simulations, developed using gpt-6.1-sol with reasoning effort set to high within the Codex harness. Integration with JAX-MD supports compiled molecular dynamics, batched replicas, walkers sharing a bias, and execution across multiple graphics processing units. We validate the framework against PLUMED and exact free energy benchmarks, and demonstrate applications to butane, silicon crystallization, and lithium transport, with severalfold improvements in computational throughput for both classical forcefields and machine learning interatomic potentials.
relevance_reason: PLUMED-JAX implements umbrella sampling and metadynamics for JAX-MD atomistic simulations with classical force fields and MLIPs, satisfying (a)-(c) as enhanced-sampling method development and application.

title: Collective dipole effects amplify field-driven ion transport in amorphous Li$_3$PO$_4$
abstract:
arXiv:2611.02617v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Amorphous solid electrolytes often outperform their crystalline counterparts, but how disorder shapes ionic transport under strong electric fields is poorly understood. We use molecular dynamics with a machine-learned interatomic potential and a machine-learned Born-effective-charge model to measure Li mobility in amorphous Li$_3$PO$_4$ and in a crystal with Li vacancies, from the linear to the strongly nonlinear regime. The amorphous phase shows a much stronger field enhancement, and we trace this to a collective dipole effect. The migrating ion carries the same charge in both phases. Alone it would not make the amorphous phase respond more strongly. What makes the difference is the environment. In the amorphous network the surrounding atoms move with the hop. Their motion makes the work the field performs vary widely between hops. Since hopping rates grow exponentially with the work, the most strongly assisted hops can dominate the drift. Disorder thus enhances field-driven transport through the environment rather than the carrier itself, a mechanism that may operate in disordered ion conductors in general.
relevance_reason: Machine-learned interatomic potential MD with a machine-learned Born-effective-charge model satisfies (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP-driven MD, and (c) application to ion transport.

title: Shadow Molecular Dynamics for General Nonlinear Flexible-Charge Models
abstract:
arXiv:2611.03499v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials have greatly expanded the reach of molecular dynamics simulations, but complex chemical environments often require explicit treatment of long-range electronic response, including charge transfer and polarization. Physics-based flexible-charge models capture these effects but require global nonlinear charge equilibration at every time step to obtain Born-Oppenheimer energies and forces. This process is computationally expensive and can lead to instabilities unless tightly converged. Here, we introduce a shadow molecular dynamics framework for flexible-charge models with arbitrary local nonlinearities and long-range multipolar electrostatics. We replace the exact Born-Oppenheimer potential with a nearby shadow potential obtained by exactly equilibrating a partially linearized electronic energy functional. This provides conservative forces and reduces the global nonlinear equilibration to a quasi-diagonal linear problem that can be solved directly at low cost. Auxiliary dynamical electronic degrees of freedom, propagated through an extended-Lagrangian dynamics, capture the long-range electronic response and define the reference state for the linearization of the energy functional. GPU-accelerated simulations with over 100,000 atoms demonstrate that the shadow potential closely follows the tightly converged Born-Oppenheimer surface, while maintaining long-term stability at a computational cost approaching that of a fixed-charge model. These advances establish an efficient and broadly applicable framework for machine-learned interatomic potentials that explicitly incorporate long-range electrostatic interactions and environment-dependent electronic response.
relevance_reason: Shadow molecular dynamics for flexible-charge models propagates explicit atoms with extended-Lagrangian dynamics and large-scale MD, satisfying (a)-(c) as classical MD method development.

title: INTERFACE Force Field for Alumina with Validated Bulk Phases and a pH-Resolved Surface Model Database for Aqueous, Electrolyte, and Molecular Interfaces
abstract:
arXiv:2601.12570v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Alumina and aluminum oxyhydroxides underpin numerous chemical engineering technologies in heterogeneous catalysis, corrosion protection, functional coatings, energy storage devices, and biomedical components. Yet molecular models that predictively connect phase structure, pH dependent surface chemistry, electrolyte organization, and adsorption across operating conditions remain limited. Here we introduce the INTERFACE Force Field (IFF) together with a curated, ready-to-use pH-resolved surface model database for an accurate and transferable atomistic description of major alumina phases according to experimental benchmarks available. The framework covers alpha-Al2O3, gamma-Al2O3, boehmite, diaspore, and gibbsite using a single parameter set compatible with CHARMM, AMBER, OPLS-AA, CVFF, and PCFF. Simulations reproduce experimental reference data across structural, thermodynamic, mechanical, and interfacial benchmarks with deviations of few percent relative to experiment, exceeding existing force fields and density-functional approaches. We introduce a transferable treatment of surface ionization and charge regulation across alumina phases over a broad pH range, enabling simulations of realistic solid-electrolyte interfaces without phase-specific reparameterization. Quantitative reliability is demonstrated by reproducing zeta-potential trends and pH-dependent adsorption of an organic corrosion inhibitor at alumina-water interfaces. Predicted adsorption free energies and surface contact times correlate with experiments across an order of magnitude, enabling process-relevant screening and explaining limitations of earlier adsorption models. The approach is 10,000 to 100,000 times faster than DFT-machine learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and supports the design of alumina-containing catalysts, corrosion-resistant coatings, energy storage and biomaterials under realistic process conditions.
relevance_reason: It introduces and validates the INTERFACE Force Field and pH-resolved surface models for alumina, with explicit atomistic simulations and classical force-field development, clearly satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Unified Learning of Interatomic Potentials and Electronic Hamiltonians, with Applications in 2D Materials
abstract:
arXiv:2510.16605v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We introduce UnIPH, an equivariant graph neural network designed to jointly predict both interatomic potentials and tight-binding (TB) Hamiltonians for an atomic structure. UnIPH is trained using density functional theory (DFT) calculations followed by Wannier projection to predict energies and forces as node-level targets and Wannier-projected TB Hamiltonians as edge-level targets. This enables physically consistent modeling of coupled mechanical-electronic responses with near-DFT-level accuracy. After separately training two UnIPH models on DFT data for bilayer graphene and monolayer MoS2, respectively, we find that these models capture key deformation-electronic effects: in twisted bilayer graphene, the trained UnIPH reveals how interlayer spacing, in-plane strain, and out-of-plane corrugation drive isolated flat-band formation, and further shows that modulating substrate interaction strength can generate flat bands even away from the magic angle (approximately 1.1 degrees). For monolayer MoS2, UnIPH accurately reproduces phonon dispersions and strain-dependent band-gap evolution, and further predicts how a non-uniform substrate creates localized strain pockets that spatially modulate the conduction- and valence-band edges.
relevance_reason: Equivariant GNN (UnIPH) jointly trained on DFT/Wannier data to predict interatomic potentials and tight-binding Hamiltonians, clearly satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP development, and (c) method advance with 2D-material applications.

title: NEVPT2 multiple spawning molecular dynamics simulations for uracil
abstract: The quasidegenerate n-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory (QD-NEVPT2) for complete active space reference wavefunctions has been implemented in the OpenMolcas package. The implementation utilizes the efficient formulation of Kollmar et al. for the electronic energy, which is extended here to the calculation of analytic derivatives. To demonstrate its utility, the method is applied to classical and non-adiabatic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of uracil. The non-adiabatic MD simulations describe the ultrafast deactivation of the initially excited bright ππ* state through the S2/S1 conical intersection, demonstrating the applicability of the method to photochemical processes. Furthermore, a machine learning-based analysis of the trajectory data extracts key geometrical parameters that are associated with the magnitude of the time-derivative coupling. These results highlight the effectiveness of this QD-NEVPT2 implementation for studying excited-state dynamics.
relevance_reason: This implements QD-NEVPT2 analytic derivatives and applies them to classical and nonadiabatic multiple-spawning MD of uracil, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) post-HF method development plus MD, and (c) excited-state dynamics application.

title: Anion Engineering Enables Concurrent Optimization of Phonon and Carrier Transport in AMg$_2$X$_2$ Zintl Thermoelectrics
abstract:
arXiv:2611.02961v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The simultaneous suppression of lattice heat transport and enhancement of carrier transport is central to the development of high-performance thermoelectric materials. Here, we investigate the microscopic mechanisms governing phonon and carrier transport in CaAl$_2$Si$_2$-type AMg$_2$X$_2$ (A = Ca, Sr, Ba; X = P, As, Sb, Bi) Zintl compounds using first-principles calculations, machine-learning interatomic potentials, and Boltzmann transport theory. As X changes from P to Bi, the widening phonon band gap restricts three-phonon scattering channels and increases the relative importance of four-phonon processes. In CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ and BaMg$_2$Bi$_2$, four-phonon scattering dominates the relaxation of low-frequency heat-carrying modes at 900 K. The Bi-based series also exhibits an anomalous increase in lattice thermal conductivity from Ca to Ba despite the increasing cation mass. Mode-resolved analysis links the lower thermal conductivity of CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ to reduced low-frequency group velocities and stronger anharmonic scattering, with Ca-related mid-frequency vibrations providing additional four-phonon scattering channels. Including both particle-like and coherent contributions, its lattice thermal conductivity reaches 0.23 W$\cdot$m$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$ at 900 K. Meanwhile, the increasing covalent character of the vertical Mg-X bonds is accompanied by enhanced band-edge dispersion and reduced carrier effective masses. These electronic changes, together with conduction-band convergence, favor n-type transport and yield a predicted peak $ZT$ of 3.68 at 900 K in CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$. These results elucidate the interplay of phonon spectral structure and higher-order anharmonicity in thermal transport, alongside the distinct electronic response to anion substitution.
relevance_reason: Trains/applies a machine-learned interatomic potential within first-principles workflows to compute phonon transport and four-phonon scattering in AMg2X2 Zintl compounds, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP development/application, and (c) applied simulation of lattice thermal transport.

title: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulation with external field
abstract:
arXiv:2611.02606v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations with classical path approximation (CPA-NAMD) cannot simulate the carrier dynamics under an external field. We develop CPA-NAMD-extF, a first-principles density-matrix framework for calculating field-driven electronic responses along precomputed finite-temperature ionic trajectories. The method combines explicit external-field coupling with self-consistent updates of electronic density while retaining the computational efficiency of the classical-path approximation. Benchmarks against regular TDDFT methods show close agreement for time-dependent dipoles, finite-field currents, and linear optical responses. Applications to the linear absorption spectrum of crystalline and amorphous SiO$_2$ demonstrate its capability to large and structurally complex systems. This method is also applied to the 2D hybrid perovskite $(\mathrm{BA})_2\mathrm{CsPb}_2\mathrm{Br}_7$. Finite-temperature calculations show that the second-order opto-current response is strongly affected by structural fluctuations. Real-space DC current density further reveals pronounced Br-centered vortex currents, and its microscopic origin is investigated.
relevance_reason: A first-principles nonadiabatic molecular dynamics framework with external field satisfies (a) explicit ionic trajectories, (b) MD/DFT methodology, and (c) method development.

title: The effect of local stacking fault fluctuations on dislocation glide and the interplay with solid solution strengthening in Al-Mg alloys
abstract:
arXiv:2611.02386v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Concentrated alloys are characterized by a random arrangement of solute atoms of different sizes, which generates spatially fluctuating displacement and stress fields with non-trivial correlations. This chemical disorder also induces local fluctuations in stacking-fault (SF) energies, giving rise to fluctuating SF forces acting on the partial dislocations bounding the SF. In this work, we investigate the characteristics of the SF noise, including spatial correlations and the impact of such SF energy fluctuations on dislocation glide. Specifically, the gliding behavior of screw, edge, and mixed dislocations in a model concentrated Al-Mg random alloy with varying Mg content is analyzed. The interplay between SF energy fluctuations and solid-solution noise is also discussed. We show that SF forces are spatially correlated, in close analogy with long-range elastic stresses, and exhibit a robust negative correlation along the slip direction. We identify the physical origin of these correlations and demonstrate that they significantly contribute to the critical resolved shear stress for dislocations to glide. In contrast, correlations in other directions are weaker but can still be non-negligible, depending on the underlying interatomic interactions.
relevance_reason: Classical atomistic simulations of dislocation glide in Al-Mg alloys satisfy (a) explicit atoms, (b) MD/force-field modeling, and (c) application to solid-solution strengthening.

title: Intermolecular and Interfacial Origins of Layering in a Near-Isotropic Organic Glass Former
abstract:
arXiv:2611.00223v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Physical vapor deposition can produce organic glasses with enhanced stability and pronounced structural anisotropy (layering) even when the constituent molecules are nearly spherical. However, the microscopic origin of the layering in spherical molecular glass formers remains unclear. We investigated vapor-deposited films of 9-(3,5-di(naphthalen-1-yl)phenyl)anthracene ({\alpha},{\alpha}-A) by grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering, atomistic molecular dynamics, and coarse-grained simulations. Experimentally, the layering signal varies nonmonotonically with deposition temperature and is strongest near 0.8T_g. Simulated scattering calculations reproduce the principal experimental features and show that the layering peak does not originate from shifts in single molecule degrees of freedom. In fact, the simulated deposited and bulk glasses show largely the same single-molecule conformations. Interestingly, a one-site coarse-grained liquid with isotropic interactions develops a comparable interfacial layering signature. These results indicate that layering in {\alpha},{\alpha}-A arises primarily from collective density correlations generated at the free surface during deposition rather than from conformational bias or orientational ordering. The findings connect structural anisotropy in vapor-deposited molecular glasses to the generic interfacial organization of simple liquids.
relevance_reason: Atomistic and coarse-grained MD of vapor-deposited organic glass formers with simulated scattering satisfies (a)-(c) as an MD application to explicit atomic systems.

title: Valence-Selective Electrophoretic Transport in Neutral Carbon Nanotubes
abstract:
arXiv:2611.02077v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Understanding how confinement alters the transport of charged molecules is central to the advancement of separation, energy, and sensing technologies. Polyamines are small, linear molecules with ionizable groups, making them an ideal model for investigating charge transport in confinement beyond monatomic ions. Using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we investigate how molecular length, net charge, and charge placement affect the electrophoretic transport of polyamines through single-walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs). We find that nanometer-scale confinement reverses the mobility ordering observed in free solution -- in a CNT of radius 0.68 nm, spermine (q = +4) travels more slowly than ethylamine (q = +1), contrasting with the expected scaling of mobility with valence in bulk. Further, we find that mobility decreases faster than the inverse of valence, though molecular size and length vary alongside this trend. Comparisons of doubly protonated spermidine microspecies reveal the additional influence of charge placement at fixed net valence. Upon moving one proton of dicationic spermidine from the central to a terminal nitrogen, the mobility is increased by 42%. We analyze hydration structure and solute-solvent association, identifying local-solvation differences between protonation topologies that accompany these distinct transport responses under confinement. These results suggest that neutral CNTs could support valence-selective nanofluidic transport, with additional sensitivity to molecular structure and protonation topology.
relevance_reason: Uses all-atom molecular dynamics to study polyamine electrophoretic transport in carbon nanotubes, directly satisfying (a)-(c) as a classical MD application.

title: All-electron Dynamical Bethe-Salpeter Equation for Extended Systems with Atom-centered Orbital Basis
abstract:
arXiv:2606.08350v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Solving Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) for the two-particle Green's function is the most widely used approach for taking into account the particle-hole (exciton) interaction in electronic excitation in the context of the many-body theory based on Green's function. In BSE calculations, the static approximation to the screened Coulomb interaction kernel is commonly employed. However, when the excitonic character is significant as typically indicated by a large exciton binding energy, dynamical screening effects become non-negligible, rendering the static approximation questionable. Because of the large computational cost due to the dense Brillouin zone integration necessary for convergence, solving the dynamical BSE for extended systems remains a significant challenge, especially when combined with GW calculation for the calculation of quasi-particle energies. In this work, we formulate the plane-wave based effective dielectric function method [Zhang, et al., Phys. Rev. B 107, 235205 (2023)] for the dynamical BSE calculation using atom-centered orbitals as basis functions. We implement this approach in our recently developed all-electron numerical atom-centered orbital (NAO) implementation of BSE@GW [Zhou, et. al. J. Chem. Theory Comput. 21, 291 (2025)] for extended systems. We validate our all-electron NAO-based implementation of the dynamical BSE method, and we then discuss its realistic application to molecular crystal of naphthalene by performing the dynamical BSE@G0W0 calculation.
relevance_reason: It develops an all-electron NAO-based dynamical BSE@GW method for extended systems, an explicit atom-centered electronic-structure method advance, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Rationalizing defect formation energies in metals and semiconductors with semilocal density functionals
abstract:
arXiv:2604.05385v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The study of defects in materials is of utmost importance for technological applications and the design of new materials. In this work, we analyze the performance of density functional approximations on two prototypical sets of defective systems: monovacancies in eight fcc metals, and interstitials in the semiconductor Si-diamond. Specifically, we compute defect formation energies using the local density approximation, the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof generalized gradient approximation, the meta-generalized gradient approximations (meta-GGAs) strongly constrained and appropriately normed (SCAN), its regularized version (r2SCAN), the Lebeda-Aschebrock-Kummel (LAK) meta-GGA, and the Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof screened hybrid functional. For metals, the local density approximation shows better performance compared to the other approximations, whereas for silicon, the meta-generalized gradient approximation Lebeda-Aschebrock-Kummel yields outstand- ing accuracy, surpassing the hybrid functional and approaching the results of more computationally demanding Quantum Monte Carlo methods. To rationalize the different performances, we study the semilocal ingredients rs, s and {\alpha} in both the pristine and defective structures. We identify critical regions that indicate the observed trends of the defect formation energies and pave the way for improving density functional approximations.
relevance_reason: It benchmarks semilocal DFT functionals for defect formation energies in metals and silicon using explicit defective atomistic cells, a DFT method assessment satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Efficient Interpolation of the Bethe-Salpeter Hamiltonian at Arbitrary Momenta
abstract:
arXiv:2611.00928v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop an efficient reciprocal-space method to reconstruct the static Bethe-Salpeter (BSE) Hamiltonian at arbitrary crystal momenta from coarse first-principles grids. Bloch states are interpolated within an optimally smooth Wannier subspace, while the screened Coulomb interaction is reconstructed from the dielectric response. This decouples the electron-hole transition momenta and transferred momentum from the underlying ab initio sampling. We benchmark the method on monolayer hBN, monolayer MoS$_2$, and bulk GaAs against explicit ab initio calculations, finding excellent agreement for dense-grid Bloch states, dielectric screening, and BSE optical spectra. Furthermore, our cost analysis estimates speedups of up to $22\times$ on the grids considered here. Arbitrary transferred-momentum sampling gives direct access to the long-wavelength exciton dispersion: in hBN and MoS$_2$, we resolve the nonanalytic behaviour induced by long-range electron-hole exchange at momenta well below the spacing of practical uniform grids. For bulk GaAs, locally refined transition-momentum sampling yields a converged binding energy for the threefold-degenerate lowest exciton, in close agreement with experiment and reference calculations, using far fewer BSE points than conventional uniform meshes. As the present framework provides exciton energies and amplitudes at arbitrary crystal momenta, it opens the way to incorporating ab initio excitonic effects into nonlocal electron-phonon vertices and to extensions towards exciton-phonon interactions and nonequilibrium exciton dynamics.
relevance_reason: Wannier/BSE interpolation method for excited-state Hamiltonians benchmarked against ab initio calculations, satisfying (a) atomistic Bloch states and (b)/(c) DFT/BSE method development.

title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface
abstract:
arXiv:2611.02723v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. Using an energy-path determination procedure, the diffusion barriers were obtained as the difference between the initial site energy and the activated complex state energy. The detachment energy of the NM adatom was obtained assuming a final state in atomic and molecular form. The energy barrier for detachment to the atomic state is high for all atoms, on the order of 5 eV. For the molecular state these barriers are different: smaller for nitrogen, on the order of 1 eV, which is related to the high dissociation energy of the N2 molecule. For P and As the barrier is above 2 eV. For Sb it was not determined. Accordingly, the surface diffusion length is macroscopically large, indicating that all NM adatoms arrive at the steps.
relevance_reason: Ab initio calculations of surface diffusion and energy barriers satisfy (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT-based pathway calculations, and (c) application to semiconductor growth.

title: Möbius-inspired signed inverse-power representations for pair-potential reconstruction, design, and RDF-driven inversion
abstract: Analytic pair potentials provide microscopic models for classical liquids, soft matter, and coarse-grained simulations. We develop a Möbius-inspired signed inverse-power representation for pair-potential reconstruction, potential-shape design, and radial distribution function (RDF)-driven inversion. The strict form uses the Möbius sequence as an arithmetic baseline. The extended form is a general signed integer inverse-power expansion with a continuous overall amplitude. It exactly represents the Lennard-Jones interaction and approximates attractive Yukawa and Morse potentials over specified radial intervals. Potential and force diagnostics establish the limits of short-range and long-range extrapolation. The same representation generates several prescribed interaction shapes and supports discrete inversion searches using shell-averaged force responses with a coordinate-derived finite-box boundary contribution. Six benchmarks span dilute and dense Lennard-Jones states and two temperatures of a repulsive Yukawa system. Independent Monte Carlo simulations reproduce their principal RDF features and selected local structural distributions, while resolving energy and pressure differences. Joint block resampling quantifies competition between nearby analytic forms. A frozen Yukawa approximation also retains close pair structure in one cross-temperature test, with measurable thermodynamic discrepancies. The results support explicit analytic pair models within stated radial and thermodynamic domains and identify the sampling and physical limitations of their structural interpretation.
relevance_reason: This develops analytic pair-potential representations and uses Monte Carlo simulations to validate RDF-driven inversion, satisfying (a) explicit-particle configurations, (b) classical force-field/pair-potential development plus MC, and (c) methodological advancement.

title: ROSE: Deep Learning exchange-correlation functional from reduced density-matrix representations
abstract:
arXiv:2611.00826v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We introduce ROSE, a deep-learning exchange--correlation energy functional built from the occupied-state density matrix. On GMTKN55 and on additional external benchmarks considered in this work, ROSE improves over modern neural network functionals trained under matched protocols and is on average more accurate than, or on par with, most hybrid and range-separated hybrid functionals considered here. On the experimental benchmarks considered here it has leading accuracy across hybrids, range separated hybrids, and neural functionals. These results motivate nonlocal density-matrix representations as a route to systematic improvement of learned XC functionals with low computational cost.
relevance_reason: Develops a deep-learning exchange-correlation functional from density-matrix representations, which is DFT method development with explicit electronic-structure/atomistic relevance, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Electric Field Gradients in Multiconfigurational Embedded-Cluster Calculations of Solids
abstract:
arXiv:2601.07098v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The electric field gradients (EFGs) at the (non-spherical) nucleus contribute to atomic and molecular hyperfine structure and govern Nuclear Electric field gradients (EFGs) at nuclei contribute to atomic hyperfine structure and govern Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance (NQR) and M\"ossbauer spectroscopy, providing a sensitive probe of local electronic structure and symmetry. EFGs can be obtained from electronic-structure calculations and inferred from spectroscopic measurements, linking theory and experiment.
  In this work, we use representative molecular and crystalline examples to examine selected factors that control calculated EFGs, with particular emphasis on multiconfigurational embedded-cluster calculations for solids. We analyze the sensitivity of EFGs to geometry and to computational choices including basis set, correlation treatment, and active-space construction. We also discuss differences in EFG tensor conventions adopted by commonly used quantum-chemistry codes and their implications for comparing computational results. Periodic calculations are used where appropriate as reference data for assessing the embedded-cluster description.
  Our results provide practical guidelines for the reliable computation and interpretation of EFGs as descriptors of the electronic structure and local chemical environment.
relevance_reason: The paper develops multiconfigurational embedded-cluster quantum-chemistry calculations of EFGs in solids, using explicit atomistic clusters and post-HF/embedding electronic-structure methodology, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Spin-Consistency Constraints in Noncollinear Tensor TDA
abstract:
arXiv:2607.19933v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: TDDFT for open-shell systems, whether spin-conserving or spin-flip, has long suffered from spin contamination. This problem arises because the single-excitation space built upon a single Kohn-Sham determinant is not spin-complete. Adopting spin tensor reference states therefore offers an elegant and promising route to resolving this issue. In this work, we revisit the tensor TDDFT equations within the Tamm-Dancoff approximation (TDA) from a noncollinear perspective. We show that, for S = 1/2 reference states, the internal consistency of the spin tensor formulation can, with the aid of the zero-excitation-energy theorem, be recast as a set of constraints that the exchange-correlation kernel must satisfy. Standard noncollinear functionals, however, generally fail to meet these constraints. To address this, we propose a kernel reconstruction scheme that is independent of the specific functional form and free of empirical parameters. This scheme enforces the required constraints, restoring internal consistency in the full spin tensor structure, with spin adaptation following as a natural consequence. Furthermore, when extended to tensor reference states with other values of S, such as S = 1 for the oxygen molecule, the scheme eliminates the so-called artifact states, namely solutions with severely underestimated excitation energies. In addition, the scheme allows the target states that ROKS reference states aim to describe to be expressed and computed, at the TDA level, within the same unified framework as other states, a capability that spin-adapted spin-conserving TDDFT has so far lacked.
relevance_reason: It develops spin-consistency constraints and kernel reconstruction in noncollinear tensor TDA/TDDFT for open-shell molecules, a DFT excited-state method advance on explicit atoms, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Ab Initio strain-dependent vibrational analysis of different silicene structures for 2D devices
abstract:
arXiv:2611.01166v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We report first-principles phonon dynamics studies in isotropically strained mono-layer silicene films of various topologies by density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory methods. The strain introduced in the sheets are of both tensile and compressive nature and its effect on the thermal transport properties are analysed using the Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE) reported. We performed electronic and vibrational analysis of each silicene topology and concluded that hhk-silicene is a potential candidate for next generation electro-thermal devices due its molecular stability, bulk-Si like bandgap and tolerable thermal performance that can be engineered by strain. The novel hhk-silicene topology offers excellent thermal and electronic capabilities that are sensitive to strain along with the band gap following a near-linear monotonically decreasing trend making it suitable for strain-tronics applications.
relevance_reason: DFT/DFPT phonon and thermal-transport study of strained silicene, with explicit atomic structures and first-principles vibrational calculations, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Atomistic Insights into MOCVD Growth of GaAs using a Closed Loop Autonomous System Combining Directed Reinforcement Learning and Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations
abstract:
arXiv:2611.01646v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conventional process optimization of the Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD) growth parameters to achieve high-quality thin films relies on iterative, resource-intensive experimental runs. While predictive modeling can circumvent this cost and effort, simulating thin-film growth is constrained by the vastly different length and time scales of the deposition process. While continuum (e.g., Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)) and first-principles methods (e.g., Molecular Dynamics (MD)) struggle to balance experimental length/time scales and atomistic accuracy, Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) bridges this divide by resolving atomistic events whilst remaining tractable at experimental length and time scales. However, the accuracy of KMC relies on kinetic rate parameters that require costly density functional theory (DFT) calculations. In order to circumvent this, we present a framework that calibrates the rate parameters directly against experimental growth data. A forward KMC growth model is coupled in a closed loop with a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) optimizer that navigates the high-dimensional parameter space, with the search steered by the degree of rate control of each reaction rate parameter. The approach invokes no material-specific assumptions and hence, any deposition process whose forward kinetics can be reduced to a set of rate-controlled events is amenable to the same treatment. We demonstrate it for the MOCVD of GaAs, where the calibrated model captures the characteristic temperature dependence of the measured growth rate. The framework is also able to recover the three well known kinetic regimes characterized by change in the rate determining step from precursor chemisorption to desorption. As a result, the framework converts routinely measured growth data into a mechanistically interpretable model of the deposition process.
relevance_reason: Kinetic Monte Carlo atomistic growth simulation coupled to reinforcement learning for MOCVD GaAs, satisfying (a) explicit atomic events, (b) MC simulation, and (c) process application.

title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
abstract:
arXiv:2611.02735v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.
relevance_reason: Ab initio calculations of step-attachment kinetics satisfy (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT energetics, and (c) application to surface growth mechanisms.

title: Transient subtraction method: An alternative approach for variance reduction in dissipative particle dynamics
abstract:
arXiv:2611.00330v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The efficient and accurate computation of transport coefficients remains a numerical challenge in dissipative particle dynamics (DPD), which can require substantial sampling to control statistical uncertainty. We extend recent results obtained in Langevin dynamics to consider the transient subtraction method for reducing the variance of transport coefficient estimations in DPD. The system is initialised by perturbing equilibrium samples, and its relaxation towards equilibrium is monitored under the reference dynamics. A reference trajectory, initialised at equilibrium and driven by the same Brownian noise, provides a control variate for the transient response. We apply the transient subtraction method to the computation of the mobility and the shear viscosity in a Lennard-Jones fluid in DPD. The shear viscosity is obtained from the time-integrated response of a Fourier observable associated with the longitudinal velocity. Numerical comparisons with the naive transient estimator show that the transient subtraction method reduces the variance at various integration times, and the reduction is more pronounced with a higher friction coefficient. These results indicate that the transient subtraction method is able to improve the statistical precision of transport coefficient estimations in DPD and reduce the number of trajectories needed to attain a prescribed standard error.
relevance_reason: Develops and validates a transient-subtraction variance-reduction estimator for dissipative particle dynamics (coarse-grained bead dynamics, a satisfied), computing mobility and shear viscosity in a Lennard-Jones DPD fluid, thus advancing an MD-type simulation methodology (b and c satisfied).

title: Fredholm approximations to the Bethe-Salpeter equation with spherical-Bessel kernels for Wannier-Mott excitons
abstract:
arXiv:2611.01570v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a deterministic radial approximation to the static Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE), designed for rapid preliminary screening of Wannier-Mott exciton binding across direct-gap bulk materials. The approximation replaces the electron-hole transition problem by small radial eigenvalue problems that require no stochastic sampling. Starting from the four-point BSE and its matrix representation in a Bloch electron-hole basis, we retain one valence and one conduction band in the effective-mass limit within the Tamm-Dancoff approximation. We introduce a central projection of the screened direct interaction and omit bare electron-hole exchange. The resulting model applies to spatially extended excitons whose envelopes vary slowly on the scale of the unit cell, provided that the effective-mass description and central screened interaction adequately represent the exciton of interest. A partial-wave decomposition separates the angular-momentum channels and expresses their interaction kernels as spherical-Bessel transforms of the real-space screened Coulomb interaction. Nystr\"{o}m discretization produces real symmetric radial matrices suitable for standard eigensolvers. Their dimension is set by the radial grid independently of the Brillouin-zone sampling used to calculate screening. We implement the formulation in the all-electron, full-potential code $\texttt{exciting}$. For bulk GaAs, the compact radial problem reproduces the corresponding conventional matrix-BSE binding energy within $(1~\mathrm{meV})$ at matched sampling. Further refinement achieves finite-mesh stability within the same tolerance on denser screening meshes without increasing the radial matrix size.
relevance_reason: Approximate BSE method with radial kernels implemented in an all-electron first-principles code for exciton binding, satisfying (a) atomistic electronic structure and (b)/(c) DFT/BSE method development.

title: Defect Chemistry of Hafnia-Based Ferroelectrics under Oxide-Electrode Constraints
abstract:
arXiv:2611.02317v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: HfO$_2$ heterostructures with La$_{0.67}$Sr$_{0.33}$MnO$_3$ (LSMO) epitaxial electrodes have attracted interest as ferroelectric systems with electrode-dependent defect chemistry. However, the formation and stability of defects under LSMO-constrained chemical conditions remain poorly understood. In this work, we use density functional theory calculations to systematically investigate oxygen vacancies and La-, Sr-, and Mn-related interstitial and substitutional defects in HfO$_2$ under chemical environments constrained by the LSMO electrode. We find that LSMO stability substantially narrows the accessible O chemical potential range relative to bulk HfO$_2$, altering the predicted defect formation energies. While La and Sr substitutional defects are governed primarily by preferred ionic valence states, oxygen vacancies and Mn substitutional defects exhibit charge states sensitive to the local atomic environment. In addition, defect-complex calculations in orthorhombic HfO$_2$ reveal negative binding energies, indicating favorable defect association. The La- and Mn-related defect complexes exhibit thermodynamic competition, with their relative stability depending on the Fermi level and oxygen chemical potential. Lastly, extending the analysis to Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$ and ZrO$_2$ reveals common oxygen-vacancy trends, while the stability of LSMO-derived defects depends more strongly on the host material and crystal phase. These results provide a thermodynamic basis for understanding how electrode-constrained chemical environments and host structures influence defect formation, charge compensation, and defect-complex stability in HfO$_2$-based materials.
relevance_reason: Density functional theory calculations explicitly model oxygen vacancies and La/Sr/Mn defects in HfO2 under electrode constraints, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT, and (c) application to defect chemistry.

title: Theoretical Prediction of Superconducting 2D Hydrogenated Janus V2CSH and Nb2CSH MXenes
abstract:
arXiv:2611.01502v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Two dimensional hydrogenated Janus MXenes represent a new frontier in superconducting materials, where asymmetric surface terminations enable tunable electronic and vibrational properties. In this work, we present the first comparative study of hydrogen or sulfur terminated V2CSH and Nb2CSH monolayers using density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory. Both compounds are structurally and thermally stable, exhibiting isotropic in plane elasticity and nonmagnetic multiband metallic states dominated by transition metal d orbitals. The asymmetric S or H terminations generate nonequivalent surface potentials and intrinsic out of plane dipoles. Electron phonon coupling constants of 0.39 (V2CSH) and 0.53 (Nb2CSH) yield superconducting transition temperatures of 2.36 K and 5.27 K, respectively, within the Allen Dynes framework. Low energy lattice vibrations, primarily involving metal and sulfur atoms, account for 77% of the coupling in both MXenes. These findings establish metal substitution as a design principle for tuning superconductivity in Janus MXenes and highlight Nb2CSH as a promising candidate for low temperature superconducting applications.
relevance_reason: DFT and density functional perturbation theory calculations of explicit Janus MXene monolayers yield phonon dispersions, electron-phonon coupling and Tc, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT/DFPT, and (c) application to predict superconductivity.

title: Pathway to lowest-energy structures and stress relaxation for the surface triple junction of copper
abstract:
arXiv:2603.01920v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The behavior of surface triple junctions (STJ) at emergent grain boundaries on free surfaces is critical to the microstructure evolution, and therefore to the stability of next generation interconnects. Yet, despite this significant importance, its lowest-energy structure and local stress have remained persistently unknown. Here, we fill this critical gap through high-resolution experimental mapping of the local surface deformation at STJs of a symmetrical tilt grain boundaries with [111] rotation axis and misorientation angles 13.17{\deg}, the analysis of the local core-shifted structure and stress relaxation, and ergodic searching metastable structures accordingly with the molecular-statics (MS) calculation. The computation clearly shows the zipped Y-shaped notch as the lowest-energy structures for this group of STJs, the line profile of which is consistent with the experimental observation. This energetic preference was well explained by the stress delocalization mechanism and was tested for a wide range of boundaries with even deeper core-shift depth using machine learning methods based on the data obtained from MS calculation. By revealing the elusive thermodynamics of STJs, our findings advance the research field by redefining the energetic framework for capillary driven structure evolution and providing foundation for understanding kinetically diffusive deformation and for engineering thin-film interconnects and related materials.
relevance_reason: Molecular-statics geometry optimization with an interatomic potential plus ML surrogate to find lowest-energy surface triple-junction structures in Cu, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) geometry optimization/force-field energetics, and (c) application to a materials system.

title: Local alternatives to Becke weights for molecular quadrature
abstract: Most density functional theory (DFT) calculations employ Becke’s methodology to partition the space in and around an n-atom molecule into n overlapping quasi-atomic regions. In this way, a single molecular integral for the energy (or other property) is reduced to a sum of n atomic integrals, each of which can then be approximated using a local grid in spherical polar coordinates. Unfortunately, the formal cost of Becke’s partition is O(n2N), where N is the total number of grid points, and this can become a computational bottleneck when applied to large molecules. We propose two modifications of Becke’s approach, each of which is formally exact and depends only on knowledge of the Delaunay neighbors of each nucleus. The two modifications can be used separately to produce schemes whose costs are O(nN) or together to produce a scheme whose cost is only O(N). Numerical tests for a variety of molecules and atomic grids suggest that the O(N) scheme should be implemented in all DFT software packages.
relevance_reason: This develops a faster Becke-weight quadrature scheme for DFT molecular integrals, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT method development, and (c) advancement of atomistic quantum-chemistry methodology.

title: Relativistic Kohn--Sham Theory of Paramagnetic Magnetic-Resonance Properties
abstract:
arXiv:2611.03170v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A general density functional theory based relativistic theory for paramagnetic NMR (pNMR) shifts, EPR g-tensors and hyperfine coupling tensors as well as magnetizabilities is derived. The formulation uses spin--orbit exact two-component (X2C) theory, gauge-including atomic orbitals, and generalized complex Kohn--Sham response equations with all ingredients being implemented analytically with the help of Goldstone modes and an orientation-constrained shielding. Additionally, we describe a two-component augmented Roothaan--Hall (ARH) solver for robust and stable convergence, which ensures that both a stationary point and a minimum are found. This is crucial for the convergence of the response equations for properties of paramagnetic systems. The extension of common population analyses for the two-component theory to aid in the interpretation of the spectra is further described. Using these new techniques, we are able to analyze the success and failure of density functional theory for relativistic open-shell systems including actinide complexes.
relevance_reason: Relativistic Kohn-Sham DFT response method development for pNMR/EPR properties on explicit open-shell complexes satisfies (a)-(c) as DFT method development, though it does not run dynamics.

title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.02906v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Generative models for crystal structure prediction (CSP) have expanded the search space for novel materials and improved screening efficiency. However, simultaneously generating stable and novel structures remains challenging because of the complex structural and physical constraints governing crystals. To address this challenge, we propose site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer model (ST2M), a symmetry-guided discrete--continuous diffusion framework incorporating degree-of-freedom masks and conditioned on Wyckoff patterns. ST2M represents crystal structures as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits and employs a twin-branch Transformer to jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables. In our experiments, ST2M achieves a structural validity of 96.37\%. For known patterns in dataset, 23.86\% of generated structures simultaneously satisfy stability, uniqueness, and novelty criteria, representing a relative improvement of 68.15\% over the best-performing baseline. First-principles calculations identify a total of 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected candidates with low predicted energies. These results demonstrate that ST2M can generate chemically viable crystal candidates under prescribed crystallographic constraints and generalize to unknown Wyckoff patterns, providing a practical route to accelerated materials discovery.
relevance_reason: Symmetry-guided diffusion model generating explicit 3D crystal structures whose candidates are validated by first-principles calculations, satisfying (a) atomistic representation, (b) DFT validation, and (c) generative CSP contribution.
